# NetFlow test fixtures (synthetic)

Everything in this directory is **synthetic**: generated by `gen_synthetic_nfcapd.sh` /
`gen_synthetic_nfcapd.py` (stdlib-only, fixed seed, fully deterministic). All IPv4 addresses are
RFC 5737 documentation addresses (192.0.2.0/24, 198.51.100.0/24, 203.0.113.0/24) or RFC 1918
private addresses (10.0.0.0/8); IPv6 addresses are RFC 3849 (2001:db8::/32); all timestamps fall
in 2001-02-03 .. 2001-02-10 UTC; the exporter Ident is `edge-router`.

The unit tests are hermetic: they never run nfdump. The nfcapd files are read only by the
classifier / review-coverage tests (4-byte magic, directory layout) and are here so the corpus can
be re-captured and so an end-to-end run inside the built image has nfcapd files to read.

## Layout

```
edge-router/                       exporter directory
  zero-length                      0-byte stray (excluded as "empty")
  2001/02/
    nfcapd.200102030000            day 1  (layout 2, 197 records)
    nfcapd.200102040000            day 2  (layout 2, 416 records)
    nfcapd.200102100600            tiny 5-minute-rotation file (5 records)
    nfcapd.200102035555            text file with a rotation-style name ("no nfdump magic")
nfdump_stdout/                     captured nfdump stdout, one file per argv shape
gen_synthetic_nfcapd.sh            regenerates everything above except the two hand-written captures
gen_synthetic_nfcapd.py            the NetFlow v5 flow catalog + UDP sender it drives
```

| File | Bytes | sha256 (first 16) |
|---|---|---|
| `edge-router/2001/02/nfcapd.200102030000` | 20780 | `e07306c1a41643b5` |
| `edge-router/2001/02/nfcapd.200102040000` | 43556 | `3904a6ae55a8694c` |
| `edge-router/2001/02/nfcapd.200102100600` | 812 | `3c46d6e7d844e32c` |

## What the corpus contains

Each pattern exercises one tool or statistic; the patterns are independent of each other.

| Pattern | Where | Numbers the tests rely on |
|---|---|---|
| Fan-out: `10.0.3.44` -> TCP/445 and TCP/3389 on 13 internal targets on two /24s (`10.0.8.21/23/27/30/34/38/41/45`, `10.0.9.12/15/19/60/66`); two SYN-only probes per target and port, a completed connection where the port answers (445 on targets 1, 4, 7, 10, 13; 3389 on targets 3, 7, 11) | day 1, 14:22:07 - 14:22:29 | 34 aggregated tuples; 74 flows (445: 41, 3389: 33); 66 SYN-only; a burst of ~22 s |
| Long-lived low-rate session `10.0.2.37:49731` -> `203.0.113.77:40519` | day 1 file, 2001-02-03 09:48:30 -> 02-04 02:48:30 | one record, exactly 61 200 s (17 h), 30 600 packets, 8 751 600 bytes = 143 B/s (1144 bit/s); nothing else on this pair |
| Periodic SYN-only retries on a pair of their own, `10.0.5.83` -> `192.0.2.150:993`, each from the next source port | day 2 file, 11:07:26 - 14:38:33 | 294 records (240 retries + 54 exporter copies), 53 s apart |
| Management traffic `10.0.4.12` -> `10.0.2.37` on TCP/22 and UDP/161 | both days | 9 records on day 1 (the host profile's inbound side) |
| Daily transfer `10.0.2.90` -> `198.51.100.23:873` | day 1 04:37, day 2 04:38 | 1 record per day |
| Proxy-style traffic: 24 clients -> `10.0.1.5:3128`, `10.0.1.5` -> three :443 destinations | both days | 30 / 22 flows on day 1 |
| ICMP and UDP/53 noise | both days | 24 ICMP, 36 UDP/53 flows on day 1 |
| Exporter duplicates | days 1 and 2 | the first 2 of every 9 records (22 %) are re-emitted with identical 5-tuple and times but 2 % more bytes (at least +1), so they are *distinct* records to an exact-duplicate filter |

`nfcapd` stamps its own wall clock into each file (header "created", every record's "received"
time); the generator overwrites both from the data (the rotation time in the file name, each
record's last-seen + 1 s), so a regenerated corpus is byte-identical.

## Regenerating

Requirements: nfdump >= 1.7 (`nfcapd` and `nfdump`) under `$NFDUMP_PREFIX` (default
`/opt/nfdump`, as in the image), Python 3.10+, `xxd`, and a free UDP port (`GEN_NFCAPD_PORT`,
default 9995).

```sh
NFDUMP_PREFIX=/opt/nfdump ./gen_synthetic_nfcapd.sh
```

The script starts a local `nfcapd` collector per bucket, sends hand-crafted NetFlow v5 export
packets to it (exact First/Last timestamps, TCP flags and counters, so every number above is exact
and reproducible), keeps the single file `nfcapd` writes, normalises its collector timestamps,
writes the two strays (`zero-length`, `nfcapd.200102035555`), and then re-captures every
`nfdump_stdout/*.txt` except the two hand-written ones below.
nfdump 1.7.10 produced the committed files; the captures were taken with `TZ=UTC`.

## `nfdump_stdout/`

Every capture is `nfdump -r edge-router/2001/02/nfcapd.200102030000 <argv>` unless noted.

| File | argv | Shape |
|---|---|---|
| `stat_ip.txt` | `-s ip/flows -n 5 -N -6 -q -o csv -- any` | STAT, `i`-prefixed columns; top row is the fan-out source (74 of 197 flows) |
| `stat_port_p.txt` | `-s dstport:p/flows -n 5 -N -6 -q -o csv -- any` | STAT with `:p` protocol split (`pr` = `6    `, `17   `) |
| `stat_multi.txt` | `-s srcip/bytes -s dstport:p/flows -n 5 -N -6 -q -o csv -- any` | two back-to-back STAT tables; the first ordered by bytes (plain columns) |
| `agg_flags.txt` | `-A srcip,dstip,dstport,flags -s record/flows -n 5 -N -6 -q -o "csv:%tsr,%ter,%sa,%da,%dp,%flg,%pkt,%byt,%fl" -- any` | AGG with `flags` as a key (the only case `%flg` is legal) |
| `agg_plain.txt` | `-A srcip,dstip -s record/bytes -n 5 -N -6 -q -o "csv:%tsr,%ter,%sa,%da,%pkt,%byt,%bps,%bpp,%fl" -- any` | AGG without `flags`; top row is the 17 h session |
| `raw.txt` | `-c 20 -N -6 -q -o "csv:%tsr,%ter,%pr,%sa,%sp,%da,%dp,%flg,%pkt,%byt" -- any` | RAW records in file order |
| `seg24.txt` | `-A srcip4/24,dstip4/24 -s record/flows -n 5 -N -6 -q -o "csv:%tsr,%ter,%sa,%da,%pkt,%byt,%fl" -- any` | SEG, /24-masked addresses |
| `dash_I.txt` | `-I` | file summary (Ident, flow/packet/byte counts, First/Last epoch) |
| `no_match.txt` | RAW argv `-- "src ip 192.0.2.99"` | header, then `No matching flows`, rc 0 |
| `no_match_stat.txt` | `-s ip/flows -n 5 -N -6 -q -o csv -- "src ip 192.0.2.99"` | `No matching flows` *before* the STAT header |
| `no_match_agg.txt` | `-A srcip,dstip,dstport -s record/flows -n 20 -N -6 -q -o "csv:%tsr,%ter,%sa,%da,%dp,%pkt,%byt,%bps,%bpp,%fl" -- "src ip 192.0.2.99"` | `-A ...` and `-s record/*` modes print *only* `No matching flows`, no header at all |
| `exit254.txt` | `-N -6 -q -o csv -- "src ip 192.0.2.99 and"` | filter syntax error on stdout, rc 254 |
| `flg_stderr.txt` | `-A srcip,dstip ... -o "csv:...,%flg,..." -- any` | `%flg` without a `flags` key: message on stderr, rc 1 |
| `sweep.txt` | `-A srcip,dstip,dstport,flags -s record/flows -n 50000 -N -6 -q -o "csv:%tsr,%ter,%sa,%da,%dp,%flg,%pkt,%byt,%fl" -- "proto tcp and flags S and dst port in [ 445 3389 ] and (src net 10.0.0.0/8 or src net 172.16.0.0/12 or src net 192.168.0.0/16) and (dst net 10.0.0.0/8 or dst net 172.16.0.0/12 or dst net 192.168.0.0/16)"` | the exact `run_netflow_sweep` argv (34 tuples) |
| `pair_retries.txt` | `-R <dir with day 1 and day 2> -c 20001 -N -6 -q -o "csv:%tsr,%ter,%pr,%sa,%sp,%da,%dp,%flg,%pkt,%byt" -- "src ip 10.0.5.83 and dst ip 192.0.2.150 and dst port 993"` | the exact `run_netflow_pair_timeline` argv for the retry pair (294 records: 240 SYN-only retries, 54 exporter copies) |
| `pair_session.txt` | the same argv with `-- "src ip 10.0.2.37 and dst ip 203.0.113.77 and dst port 40519"` | the exact `run_netflow_pair_timeline` argv for the long session's pair (one record) |
| `pair_session_both.txt` | the same argv with `both_directions=True` (`-- "((src ip 10.0.2.37 and dst ip 203.0.113.77 and dst port 40519) or (src ip 203.0.113.77 and dst ip 10.0.2.37 and src port 40519))"`), then *derived* by the generator | the capture (the session's one record) with the session's reply leg (`203.0.113.77:40519 -> 10.0.2.37:49731`, 30 600 packets, 4 590 000 bytes = 75 B/s) and its exporter copy (+2 % bytes) inserted after the session record (the corpus itself has no reply records) |
| `profile_out.txt` | `-s srcip/flows -s dstport:p/flows -s dstip/flows -s dstip/bytes -n 20 -N -6 -q -o csv -- "src ip 10.0.2.37"` | the exact `run_netflow_host_profile` outbound pass: 4 tables, table 0 is the host's own row (`flP` 100.0, the exact totals) |
| `profile_in.txt` | `-s dstip/flows -s dstport:p/flows -s srcip/flows -s srcip/bytes -n 20 -N -6 -q -o csv -- "dst ip 10.0.2.37"` | the inbound pass of the same host (the management host's 9 records on 22/tcp and 161/udp) |
| `raw_ipv6.txt` | *hand-written* | RAW shape with one full IPv6 row and one condensed (`2001:db..e0:fed5`, what nfdump prints without `-6`) row |
| `stat_flp_zero.txt` | *hand-written* | STAT shape whose top share rounds to `0.0` (the parser keeps such rows) |
